summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for bilateral native nephrectomy due to symptomatic polycystic kidney disease causing pain and limited mobility. The surgery was performed successfully, but the postoperative course was complicated by delirium, C. difficile colitis, persistent diarrhea, hypotension during hemodialysis, and postoperative ascites. She was treated with IV and oral vancomycin for C. diff, underwent paracentesis for symptomatic ascites, and was started on midodrine to improve dialysis tolerance. Atenolol was adjusted to be taken later in the day to avoid dialysis-related hypotension. She gradually improved, with resolution of infection and stabilization of volume status. She was discharged home with services on a regimen including oral vancomycin, midodrine, and adjusted antihypertensive and anticoagulant therapy, with follow-up planned for echocardiography and ongoing dialysis management.
